prompt:
You are a careful equity research analyst. Apply famous investors' frameworks to the publicly listed company "SHOPIFY INC." (ticker SHOP). Use the most recent information you know. Be specific (names, numbers, years). Never invent figures.
Reply with ONLY one JSON object:
{"summaries": { "<framework id>": "2-3 plain sentences on how well the company fits this investor's approach, written neutrally" } for EVERY framework below:
   "gardner": David Gardner: Rule Breaker Investing (The six Rule Breaker traits (Motley Fool Rule Breakers; “Rule Breakers, Rule Makers”, 1998))
   "buffett": Warren Buffett (Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letters; tenets summarised in “The Warren Buffett Way” (Hagstrom))

 "checklist": { "<id>": {"verdict": "yes|partly|no|unknown", "evidence": "one specific sentence"} } for EVERY id below (each question is shared by the frameworks that ask it):
   "momentum": Has the share price risen strongly over roughly the last six to twelve months, beating the market?
   "g4": Is it run by great leaders and backed by smart, well-known investors or partners?
   "g6": Do commentators and analysts commonly call the stock overvalued (a trait Gardner sees as a good sign)?
   "simple": Is it an established business simple enough for a careful generalist to understand well?
   "b2": Has it shown consistent results over many years?
   "integrity": Is management honest and candid with shareholders, rational with capital, paid in a way that lines up with owners, and well governed?
   "b6": Does management avoid copying peers or empire-building for its own sake?
   "roic": Does it earn a high, consistent return on the capital it uses, without relying on debt?
   "fcf": Does it turn most of its profit into plenty of free cash flow?
   "b10": Has the money it kept (instead of paying out) grown the company's value by at least as much?
   "safety": Is the share price well below a conservative estimate of the business's value (a margin of safety)?
   "fairprice": Is the price reasonable for the quality and growth on offer?
   "mu5": Thinking backwards, are there few ways this business could fail?
   "reinvest": Can it reinvest its profits at high returns for many years?

   "ly3": Is the price/earnings ratio at or below the earnings growth rate?
   "runway": Can its sales keep growing substantially for many years, into new places or products?
   "ly7": Are insiders buying and is the company reducing its share count?
   "ly8": Is it overlooked by Wall Street or in a 'boring' niche?
   "fi2": Is management committed to developing new products as current ones mature?
   "fi3": Does its R&D spending produce results?
   "fi4": Is it unusually good at selling?
   "longterm": Does management put long-term value and innovation ahead of short-term profit?
   "gr1": Is it a large, established company?
   "ni10": Has it been profitable in each of the last ten years?
   "gr4": Has it paid a dividend every year for at least 20 years?
   "eps10": Has earnings per share grown by at least one third over ten years?
   "gr6": Is the share price no more than about 15 times average earnings?
   "gr7": Is price/earnings × price/book no more than about 22.5?
   "th1": Does it have proprietary technology about ten times better than the next best?
   "timing": Is the technology and market timing right for this business now?
   "th3": Did it start with a big share of a small market, and can it expand from there?
   "team": Is it led by an exceptional founder or world-class management team?
   "th5": Does it have a way to reach and sell to customers, not just a product?
   "durable": Will its market position still hold in 10 to 20 years, resisting disruption and obsolescence?
   "th7": Has it found a unique opportunity that others don't see?
   "trend": Is it a leading beneficiary of a major platform shift or secular trend (such as AI or cloud computing)?
   "dr1": Are earnings accelerating and analysts' estimates moving up?
   "dr2": Will the business look better in 18–24 months than today, beyond what is already obvious?
   "dr4": Do interest rates, central-bank liquidity and the economy work in its favour?
   "dr6": Are there identifiable events that could drive results higher?
   "dr7": Is conviction high enough that it could be a large, concentrated position?
   "gm": Is the gross margin high, a sign of pricing power?
   "fcfyield": Is the free-cash-flow yield reasonable or attractive for its quality and growth?
   "gb2": Is operating profit high compared with the whole company's value (enterprise value)?
   "pa2": Is the business or industry going through a temporary, fixable setback?
   "pa4": Is the chance of permanent loss small even if the outcome is uncertain?
   "wo1": Is it a leader in AI, robotics, energy storage, blockchain or multiomic sequencing?
   "wo2": Are its product costs falling quickly as volumes grow, opening up big new demand?
   "wo3": Does it combine several innovation platforms?
   "wo4": Could its addressable market be many times larger in five years?
   "ac3": Is it largely insulated from commodity prices, interest rates and similar outside forces?
   "ns1": Does it pass the savings from its growing size back to customers, making it ever harder to compete with?
   "ns4": Is its likely position in 10–20 years clearly stronger than today?
   "va2": Does the product solve a large, painful problem?
   "tn1": Does it sell into a real secular trend (like AI, energy or robotics; ideally the infrastructure layer), as a company built for that trend rather than an old business retrofitting?
   "tn2": Is there a gap between the story the market tells about the company and what it is actually becoming (like Palantir seen as a consultancy, Tesla as a car company)?
   "tn3": Is it outside the zones to avoid: small caps, Chinese companies, commodity producers, airlines, seasonal businesses and startups?
   "tn4": Of these three, does it pass at least two (and have a valid reason for any miss, such as infrastructure needing leverage or a clear path to profit): revenue grown for the past few years, profitable, more cash than debt?
   "tn5": Has free cash flow been positive, and cash exceeded debt, in each of the last 4 to 6 quarters?
   "tn6": Is revenue growing at 10% a year or more?
   "tn7": Is revenue growth % plus free-cash-flow margin % at least 40?
   "tn8": Over the last year, did revenue grow faster than total operating expenses?
   "tn9": Does it avoid every instant kill: market cap under $1B, more debt than cash, short interest above 10%, operating margin below 20%, revenue growth below 10% and falling, two or more earnings misses in the last 4 quarters, or less than 10 years since founding?
   "tn10": Is it free of any major regulatory or legal threat?
   "tn11": Can it be stated plainly as “provides X that helps Y achieve Z, and charges [revenue model]”, with a clear answer to what pain it cures, who is in pain, and why customers choose it over competitors?
   "tn13": Score it on Nash's 13 categories, 0, 5 or 10 each, using the last twelve months: cash vs debt (more debt / more cash / 2x+ cash), revenue growth (<10% / 10-20% / >20%), operating margin (<10% / 10-25% / >25%), short interest (>10% / 5-10% / <5%), institutional ownership (<30% / 30-60% / >60%), revenue growing faster than expenses (no 0 / yes 10), 5-year return vs the S&P 500 (behind / ahead by 10-20% / ahead by 20%+), and, judged harshly, moat, CEO, recession-proof pricing power, secular trend, culture and mission, talent (none / some / strong). Is the total 75 or more? Give the total in the evidence.
   "tn14": Over the last five years, has revenue grown every year, operating margin expanded, free cash flow been positive and rising, and cash exceeded debt every year?
   "tn15": Would a banker lend to it: interest coverage (operating income ÷ interest) of 4x or more, assets (excluding goodwill) at least 2× liabilities, current ratio of 1 or more, and total liabilities under 4× equity?
   "tn18": Does the CEO have a track record of execution (growth, margins, innovation), skin in the game through open-market share purchases, and 10+ years in the role, ideally as founder?
   "tn20": Has it consistently beaten earnings expectations?
   "tn21": Is it free of every red flag: a clown CEO, a co-CEO structure, an acquisition spree, any suspicion of fraud or accounting problems, an auditor change, declining margins, revenue spiking while inventory piles up, or insiders selling hard while the stock runs?
   "tn22": Does it avoid the hype trap of no revenue, weak fundamentals, constant share sales to raise cash and nonstop media hype?
   "tn24": Working back from today's price, is the growth the price implies below what the company is already delivering?
   "tn25": With Nash's DCF (3-year averages of revenue growth and FCF margin, trimmed growth, 5 years of free cash flow, 4% terminal growth, plus cash minus debt), is the value per share above today's price even at a 12% discount rate?
   "tn26": Using the multiple that fits (forward P/E vs peers for mature companies, hardware and banks; Rule of 40 for software; price to sales vs the industry for unprofitable growth), is it attractive, with a PEG (forward P/E ÷ EPS growth) of 1 or less?

summaries.gardner: Shopify fits much of Gardner's Rule Breaker profile: a founder-led top dog in e-commerce software, a strong six-month share rally, and a stock widely called overvalued. Its main weakness against the traits is that its moat is good rather than unique.
summaries.buffett: Buffett would like the sticky merchant base, the debt-free balance sheet and FCF above net income, but returns on equity have been volatile and the price, about 113 times free cash flow, gives no margin of safety.
summaries.munger: Munger would value the switching costs and founder-led culture, but by inverting he would see that AI shopping agents, Amazon and fee pressure could erode it, and the valuation leaves little room for error.
summaries.lynch: Lynch would class Shopify as a fast grower with a simple story (30% revenue growth in 2025), but a P/E near 117 is far above its growth rate, it is heavily followed by Wall Street, and insiders are not buying.
summaries.fisher: Shopify scores well on Fisher's growth points: constant product development, R&D that turns into revenue growth, and long-term-minded founder management. Its gross margin has slipped as payments grew.
summaries.graham: Shopify fails most of Graham's defensive criteria: it has had losses within the last ten years, pays no dividend and trades far above 15 times earnings and 22.5 for P/E times P/B. Only its size and strong balance sheet qualify.
summaries.thiel: From a Thiel lens Shopify started by dominating a small niche (independent online stores), has a strong founder, good distribution and good timing in AI commerce. It lacks a 10x proprietary technology edge over rivals.
summaries.gerstner: Gerstner would favour its Rule of 40 profile (34% growth plus an 18% FCF margin) and its position in AI-driven commerce, while questioning whether a price of about 113 times free cash flow already reflects that.
summaries.druckenmiller: Druckenmiller would note accelerating results (operating income up 68% in Q2 2026), four straight beats and rising analyst targets as positives. Its consumer-spending exposure and rich valuation argue for caution on position size.
summaries.smith: Smith would see a good company with no debt and strong FCF conversion, but its 48% gross margin and modest returns on capital fall short of his quality bar, and the price fails 'don't overpay'.
summaries.greenblatt: By the Magic Formula Shopify ranks poorly: operating income is under 1% of enterprise value, and return on capital, while improving, is not high enough to offset that.
summaries.akre: Akre's three-legged stool fits partly: a good business with long reinvestment runway and talented founder management, but the price is far from the reasonable entry he would want.
summaries.pabrai: Pabrai's Dhandho approach seeks low risk and high uncertainty at a distressed price. Shopify is a well-understood growth story trading at a premium, so it does not fit.
summaries.wood: Shopify fits ARK's disruptive-innovation lens through e-commerce, digital wallets and agentic AI commerce, though it is a beneficiary of these platforms rather than a core technology developer.
summaries.ackman: Ackman would like a simple, predictable, debt-free platform with a dominant franchise, but its consumer-cycle exposure and a price far above his typical free-cash-flow-yield entry point are drawbacks.
summaries.sleep: Sleep would admire Shopify's scale-economies-shared ideas, such as Shop Pay and low-cost plans, and its founder's long horizon. Its 2023 price rises and falling gross margin show it does not consistently pass savings back.
summaries.valentine: Valentine would see a large, painful problem (selling online without building software) solved for millions of merchants at the right time. That kind of market-driven company is the kind he backed.
summaries.nash: Shopify passes several of Nash's tests: 30%+ revenue growth, Rule of 40, cash with no debt, strong balance sheet and a 95/130 score. It fails the 20% operating-margin instant kill and both valuation checks, with a DCF value far below the $172.50 price.

momentum.evidence: The shares rose from about $121 at end-April 2026 to $172.50 on October 14, 2026, a strong six-month run, but over twelve months they gained 14.9% versus 17.3% for the S&P 500 (SPY) to October 13, 2026.

g4.evidence: Founder-CEO Tobi Lütke has led Shopify since 2008, and it has deep partnerships with firms such as Stripe (which powers Shopify Payments) and OpenAI (checkout inside ChatGPT, announced in 2025).

g6.evidence: At about 118 times trailing GAAP earnings ($1,928M over the four quarters to June 2026) and 17 times sales, commentators routinely call it expensive; a Barchart article in August 2026 said its valuation 'leaves little room for missteps'.

simple.evidence: Selling store software plus taking a cut of payments is easy to grasp, but results also depend on payments economics, merchant lending and large swings in equity-investment values.

b2.evidence: Revenue grew every year from $2,929M in 2020 to $11,556M in 2025, but GAAP profits swing with equity-investment values: a $3,460M net loss in 2022, and a $581M net loss in Q1 2026 followed by $1,502M of net income in Q2 2026.

integrity.evidence: Lütke's letters are candid and he reversed the costly logistics push in 2023, but a Founder Share gives him outsized voting control and stock-based compensation is substantial.

b6.evidence: Shopify built and then sold its logistics business (Deliverr/Shopify Fulfillment Network) to Flexport in 2023, showing it can reverse empire-building, though it did attempt it.

roic.evidence: It has no debt and $12,684M of equity at June 30, 2026, but 2025 net income of $1,231M was only about 10% of equity and returns have been volatile.

fcf.evidence: Free cash flow of $2,007M in 2025 exceeded net income of $1,231M, an FCF margin of 17.4%, and Q2 2026 FCF was $654M (18% margin).

b10.evidence: Retained capital has funded revenue growth from $4,612M (2021) to $11,556M (2025), but the share price rose only about 26% over five years versus 79% for the S&P 500.

safety.evidence: At $172.50 the market value of about $228B is roughly 113 times 2025 free cash flow, far above conservative estimates of value.

fairprice.evidence: Even with 34% revenue growth in Q2 2026, a trailing P/E of about 117 and a PEG of about 3.7 (MarketBeat) are high for the growth on offer.

mu5.evidence: With no debt, $4,947M of cash and securities and sticky merchants, a collapse is unlikely, but AI-led shopping, Amazon and payment-fee pressure are real failure paths for its growth.

reinvest.evidence: Commerce software needs little capital, and Shopify keeps finding new areas (enterprise, B2B, POS, international, agentic commerce) while growing revenue above 30%.

ly2.evidence: It is a clear fast grower: revenue up 30% in 2025 and 34% in Q2 2026, with a simple story of taking more of global commerce.

ly3.evidence: A trailing P/E of about 118 is far above its roughly 30% revenue growth rate.

runway.evidence: GMV of $378.4B in 2025 is a small fraction of global retail, and it is expanding into enterprise, offline POS, B2B, international and AI channels.

ly7.evidence: Insiders made no open-market purchases in the past three months (MarketBeat), and diluted shares rose from 1,295.5M in 2023 to 1,305.0M in 2025.

ly8.evidence: Around 48 analysts cover the stock and it is one of the most widely followed technology names.

fi2.evidence: It ships hundreds of features twice a year in its 'Editions' releases and has added Shop Pay, POS, Shopify Capital, B2B and agentic checkout over time.

fi3.evidence: Its product spending has produced fast growth: revenue rose from $7,060M in 2023 to $11,556M in 2025 and MRR from $178M to $221M by Q2 2026.

fi4.evidence: Its self-serve sign-ups, free trials and partner/app ecosystem attract millions of merchants efficiently, but its enterprise sales force is newer and still winning share against Salesforce and Adobe.

longterm.evidence: Lütke runs it for the long term, investing heavily in AI and new products and emphasising decades-long thinking in his letters.

gr1.evidence: It is a large company with $11,556M of revenue in 2025 and a market value of about $228B.

ni10.evidence: It lost money in several of the last ten years, including a $3,460M net loss in 2022.

gr4.evidence: Shopify has never paid a dividend.

eps10.evidence: Earnings moved from losses in the mid-2010s to $1,231M of net income in 2025, but the path was erratic, with a $3,460M loss in 2022.

gr6.evidence: The share price is about 118 times trailing GAAP earnings ($1,928M of net income over the four quarters to June 2026), far above 15.

gr7.evidence: A P/E of about 117 times a price-to-book of about 17.9 gives roughly 2,100, far above 22.5.

th1.evidence: Its software and checkout are excellent, but not ten times better than rivals such as BigCommerce, Wix, WooCommerce or Salesforce Commerce.

timing.evidence: Commerce keeps moving online and into AI assistants, and Shopify launched checkout inside ChatGPT in 2025 just as agentic shopping began.

th3.evidence: It began serving small independent online stores, came to dominate that niche, and has expanded to enterprise brands, POS, payments and lending.

team.evidence: Founder Tobi Lütke has run it since 2008 alongside President Harley Finkelstein, growing revenue to $11,556M in 2025.

th5.evidence: Free trials, the Shop app, a large partner and agency network and an enterprise sales team give it strong ways to reach merchants.

durable.evidence: Switching costs and its ecosystem should hold for a long time, but AI shopping agents and Amazon could shift where purchases start and who controls checkout.

th7.evidence: Its 'arm the rebels' bet that brands would want their own stores rather than Amazon was contrarian, though the opportunity is now widely recognised.

trend.evidence: It is a leading beneficiary of the shift to online and AI-driven commerce, with GMV up 32% in Q2 2026 to $115.6B.

dr1.evidence: Operating income rose 68% to $488M in Q2 2026 (from $291M), aggregator data (Benzinga) show four straight beats against consensus, and analysts raised targets in October 2026 (Stifel to $210, Baird to $190, JPMorgan to $200).

dr2.evidence: Margin gains and agentic commerce could make it look better in two years, but much of that hope is already reflected in the share price.

dr4.evidence: It has no debt, but its results depend on consumer spending, and tariffs and the end of the US de minimis exemption hurt some small merchants.

dr6.evidence: Q3 2026 results in early November, the holiday shopping season and checkout in AI assistants are clear potential catalysts.

dr7.evidence: The business quality supports conviction, but at about 113 times free cash flow the valuation risk argues against a very large position.

gm.evidence: Gross margin was 48.1% in 2025, down from 53.8% in 2021, low for software because payments make up most revenue.

fcfyield.evidence: 2025 free cash flow of $2,007M against a market value of about $228B is a yield of about 0.9%.

gb2.evidence: 2025 operating income of $1,468M is only about 0.7% of its roughly $223B enterprise value.

pa2.evidence: Shopify is not in a setback: revenue grew 34% and operating income 68% in Q2 2026.

pa4.evidence: The balance sheet ($4,947M of cash and securities, no debt) limits business risk, but at about 117 times earnings a growth slowdown could cause lasting losses for buyers.

wo1.evidence: It is an aggressive AI adopter and a leader in agentic commerce, but it is not a core AI, robotics or blockchain platform company.

wo2.evidence: Its scale lowers payment and infrastructure costs per merchant, but it has not shown the steep, Wright's-law cost declines that ARK looks for.

wo3.evidence: It combines e-commerce, digital payments (Shop Pay) and AI-driven shopping, overlapping some of ARK's platforms.

wo4.evidence: Its market can keep growing fast, but GMV of $378.4B in 2025 is unlikely to become many times larger in five years.

ac3.evidence: It has no debt and no commodity exposure, but revenue depends on consumer spending, and interest income and payment volumes move with the economy.

ns1.evidence: Shop Pay, cheap starter plans and growing scale help merchants, but Shopify raised subscription prices in 2023 and gross margin fell from 53.8% (2021) to 48.1% (2025).

ns4.evidence: Growing GMV and merchant lock-in point to a stronger position, but AI-driven shopping makes its 10 to 20 year position less certain.

va2.evidence: It solves a large, painful problem: letting anyone launch and run a store with payments, shipping and checkout without building software.

tn1.evidence: It is built for the e-commerce trend and is moving into agentic AI commerce, but it is a commerce platform rather than AI or energy infrastructure.

tn2.evidence: The market still largely sees a store-builder, while about three-quarters of revenue now comes from merchant services, mainly payments, and it is building an AI-commerce layer.

tn3.evidence: It is a $228B large-cap, Canadian-headquartered company founded in 2006, not a commodity, airline, Chinese or startup business.

tn4.evidence: It passes all three: revenue grew every year since 2020, net income was $1,231M in 2025 and $1,928M over the four quarters to June 2026 (despite a $581M Q1 2026 loss driven by equity investments), and $4,947M of cash and securities sits against no borrowings.

tn5.evidence: Shopify reported positive free cash flow in each of the last four quarters ($507M Q3 2025, $715M Q4 2025, $476M Q1 2026, $654M Q2 2026), and it has had no borrowings since its convertible notes matured in 2025, against $4,947M of cash and securities at June 30, 2026.

tn6.evidence: Revenue grew 30% in 2025 and 34% in Q2 2026.

tn7.evidence: Q2 2026 revenue growth of 34% plus an 18% FCF margin gives 52, and 2025 gives 30% + 17.4% = 47.

tn8.evidence: In Q2 2026 revenue rose 34% while operating expenses rose 20.7% ($1,011M to $1,220M).

tn9.evidence: It fails on operating margin: 12.7% in 2025 and 13.6% in Q2 2026, below 20%.

tn10.evidence: There is no existential legal threat, but it faces privacy class actions in the US and policy risks such as tariffs and the end of the de minimis exemption.

tn11.evidence: Shopify provides commerce software and payments that help merchants of every size sell online and in person, charging subscriptions plus a percentage of payments, and merchants choose it for ease of use, its app ecosystem and Shop Pay conversion.

tn13.evidence: Total about 95 of 130: cash vs debt 10, revenue growth 10, operating margin 5, short interest 10 (1.57%), institutional ownership 10 (69%), revenue faster than expenses 10, 5-year return vs S&P 500 0 (+26% vs +79%), moat 5, CEO 10, pricing power 5, secular trend 10, culture 5, talent 5.

tn14.evidence: Revenue grew every year, but there were operating losses in 2022 and 2023, so operating margin did not expand steadily.

tn15.evidence: With no borrowings it has no interest burden, assets excluding goodwill of $13,979M are about 7.8 times liabilities of $1,786M, current assets ($7,816M) exceed all liabilities, and liabilities are 0.14 times equity.

tn18.evidence: Lütke has been CEO since 2008 as founder with a strong record of growth and innovation, but there is no record of open-market share purchases.

tn20.evidence: Shopify's reported revenue rose each quarter ($2,844M Q3 2025, $3,672M Q4 2025, $3,170M Q1 2026, $3,583M Q2 2026), and aggregator Benzinga's data show adjusted EPS and revenue beating consensus estimates in all four quarters (e.g. $3.58B vs a $3.44B estimate in Q2 2026); the estimates come from that aggregator, not the company.

tn21.evidence: There is no fraud, auditor change or acquisition spree, but gross margin has declined from 53.8% (2021) to 48.1% (2025).

tn22.evidence: It is no hype stock: $11,556M of 2025 revenue, $2,007M of free cash flow and no need to sell shares to raise cash.

tn24.evidence: A reverse DCF on its ~$223B enterprise value (10% discount, 3% terminal growth) implies about 31% annual FCF growth for ten years, roughly its current revenue growth sustained for a decade, not below it.

tn25.evidence: Using 27% average 3-year revenue growth (trimmed to about 20%), a ~17% FCF margin, 4% terminal growth and a 12% discount rate gives roughly $40 to $55 per share, far below $172.50.

tn26.evidence: It passes the Rule of 40 (34% growth + 18% FCF margin = 52), but with a forward P/E of roughly 69 to 118 depending on source and a PEG of about 3.7 it fails the PEG-of-1 test.
